records.title: What Is a Watchlist?
records.topic: Issuer identity and time-stamped research records
records.objective: Separate the learner's watchlist research record from any recommendation to trade and verify the issuer's identity before interpreting a symbol.
records.claim: The SEC uses a Central Index Key (CIK) to identify companies and individuals that file disclosures. A ticker or marketing nickname alone is insufficient to establish the legal filing issuer.
records.sourceClaim: The SEC uses CIKs to identify EDGAR filers; a company may have name variants.
records.worked: FICTIONAL: A research row says ticker QXY, but a promoter references renamed ticker QXZ. Record legal issuer, share class, CIK, as-of timestamp and authoritative original filing link before evaluating the claim. A missing identity results in RESEARCH PENDING, not BUY.
records.calculation: Evidence procedure: (1) capture the claimed symbol and time; (2) search the SEC CIK lookup by actual legal issuer; (3) check EDGAR CIK and any name/symbol chronology; (4) separate verified issuer identity from the unverified promotion; (5) document a no-trade decision if unmatched.
records.counterexample: A watchlist entry with a quoted price and three news reposts, but no original issuer record, has duplicated promotion rather than three independent sources. A correct ticker at one date does not establish the issuer at another.
records.transfer: FICTIONAL independent case: ticker ABCX became ABCY yesterday, while the only disclosure uses a matching CIK but a different share class. Explain why source chronology, CIK, and share class must be reconciled before an alert is classified as a real catalyst.
records.limit: The SEC does not certify the owner's watchlist method, stock choice, trading performance or any fictional issuer. A CIK is an identifier, not a validation of a promotional claim.

records.title: Finding the Real Catalyst
records.topic: Original issuer announcement versus promoter repost timing
records.objective: Verify the original issuer source, timestamp, filing type and material condition before treating a repost as a catalyst.
records.claim: SEC EDGAR allows research of actual issuer disclosures, including periodic and event-oriented filings. An amended filing is labeled with /A; a promotional report is not interchangeable with the original issuer record.
records.sourceClaim: EDGAR displays actual reporting company filings, categorized by form type and amendment.
records.worked: FICTIONAL: at 08:10 ET a promotional post claims a completed $5 million contract; the source filing visible at 08:25 ET describes only a conditional proposal. The earlier post cannot establish that the contract was completed at 08:10.
records.calculation: Evidence chronology: promotional claim at 08:10, source available at 08:25, decision boundary at 08:15. Source-after-pause = 10 minutes later, so it cannot justify an earlier conclusion. Identify whether the statement is conditional, executed or recognized revenue.
records.counterexample: A popular repost using the issuer's correct symbol is still secondary. A filed Form 8-K does not mean SEC endorsement, proof of a market reaction, or proof that a nonbinding agreement became unconditional.
records.transfer: FICTIONAL: a press headline at 07:55 ET claims a $12 million sale, but the first available issuer document at 08:07 ET describes a memorandum of understanding with termination conditions. At 08:00 ET decide what can be asserted and what must remain unresolved.
records.limit: SEC filings document disclosures, not historical tape, verified investor awareness, broker executions, revenue recognition or a forecastable return. Publication versus acceptance timing may require separate corroboration.

records.title: Volume and relative volume
records.topic: Matched-interval RVOL calculation and scanner false positives
records.objective: Calculate relative volume with a documented denominator drawn from comparable intervals, and reject mismatched interval comparisons.
records.claim: StockCharts ChartSchool distinguishes typical session-level relative volume from time-of-day relative volume, which compares equivalent intraday intervals across sessions.
records.sourceClaim: RVOL-TOD compares a five-minute bar with previous bars for the same time of day; data window and platform method vary.
records.worked: FICTIONAL: a current five-minute bar trades 8,000 shares. Someone divides by a 2,000-share daily statistic and declares 4x RVOL; the units and interval are mismatched. Against comparable 9:30–9:35 five-minute bars averaging 10,000 shares, valid illustrative RVOL-TOD is 8,000/10,000=0.80x.
records.calculation: RVOL-TOD = current bar shares / mean shares for aligned past bars with the same time-of-day and bar length. Both numerator and denominator are shares in five-minute intervals; missing bars, feed coverage, holidays and sample window must be disclosed.
records.counterexample: An apparent 4x volume spike caused by comparing a five-minute bar to an unrelated daily or premarket denominator is not evidence of exceptional participation and is not an independently verified profitable scan.
records.transfer: FICTIONAL: a completed 09:30–09:35 five-minute bar has 12,000 shares and the average of matched historical 09:30–09:35 five-minute bars is 6,000 shares. Calculate 2.00x and name two additional inputs needed before interpreting liquidity or tradability.
records.limit: The ChartSchool explanation does not verify a vendor scanner result, current live market feed, trading signal or strategy edge. Original ratios are arithmetic examples, not market observations.
